chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Mithammi, from his two brothers, Muhammad and Ahmad, from Ali ibn Yaqoub al-Hashimi, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Saeed ibn Amr al-Ju'fi, from a man from the people of Egypt, who said:

My brother bequeathed to me a slave girl who was a singer for him, a luxury, and made her a gift (hadya) to the Sacred House of Allah. So I arrived in Mecca and asked, and it was said to me, 'Hand her over to the Banu Shayba,' and other words were said to me, so there was conflict regarding it. A man from the people of the Masjid said to me, 'Shall I guide you to one who will guide you to the truth in this?' I said, 'Yes.'

He said, 'So he pointed to an old man sitting in the Masjid and said, 'This is Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), so ask him.' I said, 'So I went to him (peace be upon him) and asked him, and related the story to him.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, the Ka'bah neither eats nor drinks, and whatever is gifted to it is for its visitors. Sell the slave girl, and stand on the Hajar al-Aswad and call out: Is there one who has been cut off (by bandits), and is there one who is needy among its visitors? When they come to you, ask about them, give to them, and distribute her price among them.'

He said, 'So I said to him, 'Some of those I asked instructed me to hand her over to the Banu Shayba.' He said, 'But, our Qaim (the Imam), if he had risen, would have seized them, cut off their hands, circled with them, and said: These are the thieves of Allah.'

key_terms.بَنِي شَيْبَةَ: The Banu Shayba clan, custodians of the Ka'bah
key_terms.هَدْياً: Gift or offering, specifically for the Ka'bah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on gifts given to the Ka'bah and who receives them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential principle that gifts dedicated to the Ka'bah (hadya) are not consumed by the structure itself but belong to its visitors (zuhhur), specifically the needy pilgrims. Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates this by instructing the sale of a gifted slave girl and distributing the proceeds, while also contrasting the current custodians' management with the future authority of the Qaim, who will hold the Banu Shayba accountable for their stewardship. This narrative underscores the Shia view of the Ka'bah as a center for social welfare and divine justice rather than a static religious monument.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from his two brothers, Muhammad and Ahmad, from Ali Bin Yaqoub Al Hashimy, from Marwan Bin Muslim, from Saeed Bin Amro Al Ju’fy, from a man from the people of Egypt who said,

‘My brother bequeathed to me with a slave girl who was a singer for him, a luxury, and made her to be gifted to the Sacred House of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So I proceeded to Makkah and asked around. So it was said, ‘Hand her over to the Clan of Shayba’, and it was said to me other than that from the words. So it was conflicting upon me with regards to it. So a man from the people of the (Sacred) Masjid said to me, ‘Shall I guide you to the one who would guide you regarding this, to the Truth?’ I said, ‘Yes’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he indicated towards an old man seated in the Masjid and he said, ‘This is Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> Bin Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>, so ask him<sup>asws</sup>’. So I went over to him<sup>asws</sup> and asked him<sup>asws</sup>, and related the story to him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Kabah neither eats nor drinks, and whatever is gifted to it, so it is for the visitors. Sell the slave girl and stand upon the (Black) Stone and call out, ‘Is there one who has been cut-off (by the bandits), and is there one who is needy’, from its visitors. So when they come over, so ask about them, and give them, and distribute her price among them’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘One of the ones I asked instructed me with handing her over to the Clan of Shayba’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup>, if he<sup>asws</sup> had risen, would have seized them, and cut off their hands, and circled with them and said: ‘These are the thieves (stealing from) Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from Ah ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from his two brothers Muhammad and Ahmad from Ah ibn Ya’qub al-Hashimiy from Marwan ibn Muslim from Sa‘id ibn ‘Umar al-Ju’fiy from a man from people of Misr (Egypt) who has said the following:

“My brother in his will made a beautiful singer slave-girl a gift to the Bayt of Allah al-Haram (the Sacred House of Allah). I then went to Makkah and asked about it. I was told to give her to banu Shaybah. In addition, other things were said to me. It became confusing to me. One man from the Masjid asked me, ‘Can I show someone who can instruct you in this matter of rights?’ I replied, ‘Yes, please do so.’

He showed me a shaykh who was sitting in the Masjid and said, ‘This is Ja’far ibn Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Ask him your question.’ I then went to him (the Imam), asked my question and explained to him the story. He (the Imam) said, ‘Al-Ka‘bah does not eat and drink, so whatever is given as gift to al-Ka‘bah is for those who visit al-Ka‘bah. Sell the slave-girl, stand up near the Black Stone and announce, “Those looted on the way and any needy of the visitors of al- Ka‘bah (can come to me).” Distribute the amount among them.’

I then said, ‘Certain people have told me to give it to banu Shaybah.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘When it is the rise of our al-Qa’im with divine authority, he will arrest them, cutoff their hands and make them walk (among people); they are thieves who steal from Allah.’”
